title: Plural yes/no questions: Ovatko nämä…?
summary: Build affirmative plural yes/no questions with ovatko.
objectives: Begin a plural affirmative question with ovatko.
Keep the supplied plural subject unchanged.
Contrast plural ovatko with singular onko.

sections.title: See the pattern
paragraphs: A plural affirmative yes/no question begins with Ovatko.
Ovatko combines ovat with the question suffix -ko.

sections.title: Use one clear decision
paragraphs: The demonstrative and supplied noun remain plural after it.
Read the subject number before choosing the question verb.

steps: nämä laukut: the complete subject is supplied.
nuo laukut: the complete subject is supplied.
ne laukut: the complete subject is supplied.

commonMistakes: Do not use onko with a plural subject.
Do not change the supplied plural noun.
Do not place ovatko after the subject.

practiceExercises.instruction: Put the words in the correct order.
practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Build “Are the keys at home?” Use ne avaimet (“the keys”) and kotona (“at home”).
practiceExercises.explanation: Ovatko adds -ko to ovat, the olla form for several things. In English, begin the question with “Are” before the subject.

optionFeedback.Ovatko nämä kirjat täällä?: Correct. Ovatko is the plural olla form with the question suffix -ko.
optionFeedback.Onko nämä kirjat täällä?: “Onko” is the singular affirmative question verb; use “Ovatko”, the plural affirmative question verb.
“Ovat” is the plural affirmative form of olla; use “Ovatko”, the plural affirmative question verb.
optionFeedback.Eivätkö nämä kirjat ole täällä?: “Eivätkö” is the plural negative question verb; use “Ovatko”, the plural affirmative question verb.
